Population.evidence_source: The decedents purposively indulged in alcohol, possibly to intoxicate themselves to death. The following voices seem to allude to this assertion: ". . . he could go days without even eating food and his only talk could be 'I should drink up to death' and yet he never used to drink that much" (case14:informant2).

Area.evidence_source: Statements such as "I should drink up to death," "they should leave alcohol to kill me," and "let alcohol kill me before . . ." seem to imply that alcohol was reflected on as a method of suicide. The decedents purposively indulged in alcohol, possibly to intoxicate themselves to death. ... This particular quote implies that the harsh conditions in the army drove him into drinking, possibly as a way of coping. Even then life continued being hard, and he eventually decided to desert, but he could be arrested at any time and taken back. He thus preferred alcohol to kill him rather than facing the wrath that would follow if he were arrested.
